neighbours.label: a person's body part or family-role noun after 'the' in narrative (the cheek, the shoulder, the mom, the older brother)
fire: He leaned in and gently kissed her on the forehead before saying goodbye.
The ball struck him squarely in the knee and he crumpled to the grass.
She wiped a tear away from the corner of her eye with one finger.
Their grandmother always gave the youngest grandson an extra slice of cake.
At the wedding, the bride's father gave a long and teary speech.
He grabbed the little girl by the hand and pulled her across the street.
The teenager rolled his eyes when the dad started dancing in the kitchen.
My sister kept poking me in the ribs during the whole movie.
quiet: He leaned in and gently placed the vase on the windowsill before leaving.
The ball struck the fence squarely and bounced back onto the grass.
She wiped the dust away from the corner of the frame with one finger.
Their bakery always gave the youngest customers an extra slice of cake.
At the wedding, the band played a long and lively set of songs.
He grabbed the heavy suitcase by the handle and pulled it across the street.
The teenager rolled the cart back when the store started closing for the night.
My friend kept tapping the table during the whole movie.

notes: Common pattern: relational nouns that belong to a person (body parts, kin roles), not objects.
